transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because things have been getting really confusing lately with my work. My artist statements and my client notes... people keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. Which is honestly so frustrating because I spend a lot of time on those notes. I actually buy this really specific, expensive paper for them. It's handmade in Italy, cold-pressed, and it has this beautiful deckled edge. I found this little shop downtown that sells it, right next to a bakery that makes just the absolute worst scones. Have you ever had a really dry scone? It's like eating sand, I don't know how they stay in business. 

But anyway, yeah, the notes. And it's not just what I write, it's what I say in meetings, too. I guess I've started jumping around a lot. Like, I'll be talking about the textures of a piece, and then suddenly I'm talking about the budgets, and then I get into the secret meanings behind the project... and everyone just kind of stares at me because they have no idea how I got from point A to point B.
During these times when your thoughts and speech feel disorganized, have you also been experiencing an unusually elevated or irritable mood, or a significantly decreased need for sleep?

Yeah, actually... yes. For stretches I'll feel completely lit up. Like I am almost unstoppable and every single idea that pops into my head is just brilliant. Like, last week I had this concept for a mixed-media piece using crushed lapis lazuli. Did you know lapis was more expensive than gold during the Renaissance? They used it for the Virgin Mary's robes in all those old paintings. I saw this documentary about it, and how the apprentices had to grind the pigments by hand. It sounds exhausting, honestly, just grinding rocks all day. I prefer buying my paints pre-mixed, though there is this one shop that sells raw pigments in these tiny glass jars. They look exactly like spices in a pantry. I love cooking with lots of spices, especially cumin. Cumin smells like... well, it smells like a really good taco truck. There's one down my street that makes amazing al pastor, they put the little pineapple slice on top and everything. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, my mood. Right. So I'll be feeling brilliant and unstoppable like that, but then... if a collaborator makes even a small comment about my work, I just snap. Like, I lash out in a way that feels way bigger than the situation. It just happens so fast.
Have you ever had these periods where your thoughts are disorganized or you feel like people aren't following you even when you are NOT feeling that 'lit up' or 'unstoppable' mood?

Yeah, I have. Like... maybe a few months ago, there was this whole month where things were actually pretty quiet. I was sleeping a normal amount, not staying up all night, and I definitely didn't have that supercharged, brilliant feeling. I was just kind of... there. But even then, I was still having trouble. I kept hearing these comments, like whispers, coming from behind the shelves in my studio. My studio has these huge metal industrial shelves, the kind you get at a hardware store. I had to assemble them myself and I lost one of the little bolts, which is so annoying because now one of the shelves is just slightly wobbly. You know when a table at a restaurant wobbles and you have to put a sugar packet under it? I hate that. I always end up spilling water.

But anyway, yeah, even without feeling elevated, I was hearing those comments for weeks. And I was also finding these... hidden warnings in my regular studio materials. Like the way the paint tubes were arranged, or the labels on the solvents, they felt like they were trying to tell me something dangerous was going to happen. So, yeah, it still happens even when my mood isn't all over the place.
Looking back at the past six months, would you say that you have spent more time feeling that 'lit up' or 'unstoppable' way, or more time feeling like your normal self?

Well, if I really think about the last six months... I'd say the lit-up, unstoppable stretches have definitely taken up way more time. It's like, even though the intensity kind of goes up and down, that energized, irritable, overproductive feeling has been the main thing for most of the year. It's honestly exhausting, but I get so much done. I actually just finished this massive canvas, it's like six feet tall. I had to buy a special ladder just to reach the top corners. It's one of those aluminum ones that folds out into different shapes, you know? My dad has one exactly like it, he uses it to clean the gutters at his house. His house is this old Victorian, painted this really weird shade of mustard yellow. I don't know why they picked that color, it clashes so badly with the green trim. It looks like a hot dog with too much relish. Relish is so gross, honestly, just chopped up pickles in syrup. Why would anyone want sweet pickles? Pickles should be sour and garlicky. 

But yeah, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the time. Yeah, definitely more time feeling energized and on edge than feeling like my normal self, for sure.
